summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY with embedded firmware experience in C and C++ on STM32 microcontrollers, Arduino and Raspberry Pi. Debugged hardware with oscilloscopes and logic analyzers, designed EAGLE PCBs, and applied machine learning (PyTorch, TensorFlow) on embedded platforms.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth, translating 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning (root cause analysis).
Produced technical documentation and a BOM for an AI-based Mixed Reality headset concept.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.
Organized 10+ exhibitions and technical workshops covering Arduino, PCB design, and SolidWorks; authored and taught a Python course (syllabus, syntax booklet, coursework).

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Developed a Python GUI (PyQt, Matplotlib) for real-time data acquisition in a lab; used GitLab and JupyterHub for version control and technical documentation.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built Cortex-M4 firmware in bare-metal embedded C on an STM32 microcontroller, hitting 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate; verified in Proteus.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver; programmed GPIO, TIM2, ADC1 and I2C1 directly.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Built a voice-controlled, vision-guided pick-and-place system across a Flutter client, Flask-SocketIO edge server, and Jetson+Arduino controller on a unified WebSocket fabric; achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials).
Integrated TensorRT-optimized YOLO (5.2× speedup: 56.7→10.9 ms) and dual VL53L0X ToF sensors over a TCA9548A I2C mux; implemented two-link IK on Arduino in C++.
Resolved 11 integration failures (servo brown-out, stale frames, false positives); deployed the arm bridge as a systemd service with static IP networking.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, sending control commands to an STM32 microcontroller over UART.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART and FreeRTOS mutexes for task coordination.
